subject: ss-cardiology
title: Antiarrhythmic drugs: classes, proarrhythmia and the agents exams ask about

steps.tx: The **Vaughan Williams** scheme groups drugs by the current they block. Class 1 drugs block fast sodium entry: class 1a quinidine and procainamide, class 1b lidocaine and mexiletine, and class 1c flecainide and propafenone. Class 2 drugs are beta blockers. Class 3 drugs are **potassium channel blockers** such as amiodarone, sotalol and dofetilide. Class 4 drugs, verapamil and diltiazem, slow the L type calcium current. The ventricular action potential shows where those currents sit.
steps.say: The Vaughan Williams scheme groups antiarrhythmic drugs by the current they block. Class 1 drugs block fast sodium entry, class 2 drugs are beta blockers, class 3 drugs block potassium channels, and class 4 drugs slow the L type calcium current. The ventricular action potential diagram shows where those currents sit during the spike and during recovery.

vis.alt: Diagram of a ventricular myocyte action potential beside a sinoatrial pacemaker potential, with sodium, calcium and potassium currents.
vis.caption: Cardiac action potential currents that Vaughan Williams classes block. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **CAST trial** tested flecainide and encainide after myocardial infarction and found more deaths, not fewer. Class 1c sodium block binds tightly in scarred muscle, slows conduction, and lets re entry sustain. That is why class 1c drugs are avoided in **structural heart disease**, a prior infarct, or a reduced ejection fraction. They remain options only for selected patients with a normal heart and atrial fibrillation, after ischaemia has been excluded.
steps.say: The CAST trial tested flecainide and encainide after myocardial infarction and found more deaths, not fewer. Class 1c sodium block slows conduction inside scar and lets re entry continue. That is why these drugs are avoided in structural heart disease, a prior infarct, or a reduced ejection fraction.

left.title: Class 1c, normal heart
points: Flecainide or propafenone may be considered for atrial fibrillation when the ventricle and the coronaries are normal.
Still watch for atrial flutter with 1 to 1 conduction, and combine with a drug that slows the node.

right.title: Class 1c, scar or weak ventricle
points: CAST showed higher mortality after infarction.
Do not use flecainide or propafenone in structural heart disease or heart failure.

steps.tx: **Amiodarone** carries a piece of all 4 Vaughan Williams classes, which is why it can hold sinus rhythm when other drugs fail, including in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The cost is cumulative organ injury: **pulmonary fibrosis**, thyroid disease, corneal deposits, hepatitis and slate grey skin. Thyrotoxicosis splits into type 1, iodine driven and hypervascular, and type 2, a destructive thyroiditis. Check thyroid, liver, lungs and eyes, and the QT, for as long as the drug continues.
steps.say: Amiodarone carries a piece of all four Vaughan Williams classes and can be continued in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The cost is cumulative injury to lung, thyroid, liver, cornea and skin. Thyrotoxicosis is either an iodine driven hypervascular gland or a destructive thyroiditis. Surveillance continues for as long as the patient takes the drug.

vis.alt: Two thyroid glands: a hypervascular goitre from iodine excess, and a destroyed gland with absent blood flow from amiodarone thyroiditis.
vis.caption: Amiodarone thyrotoxicosis, type 1 iodine excess versus type 2 destructive thyroiditis. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Dronedarone** was built as an amiodarone analogue without iodine, so thyroid and lung toxicity are less of the story. It is not a safer amiodarone for sick hearts. **ANDROMEDA** stopped early because deaths rose in decompensated heart failure, and PALLAS showed harm in permanent atrial fibrillation. Those two groups are strict contraindications. In a patient with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a stable ventricle, dronedarone is only one option among rhythm drugs, not the default in heart failure.
steps.say: Dronedarone was built as an amiodarone analogue without iodine, so thyroid and lung toxicity are less prominent. ANDROMEDA stopped early because deaths rose in decompensated heart failure, and PALLAS showed harm in permanent atrial fibrillation. Those two situations are strict contraindications.

left.title: Amiodarone
points: Iodinated. All 4 classes. Used in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction when a rhythm drug is required.
Lung, thyroid, liver, cornea and skin need a schedule of checks.

right.title: Dronedarone
points: No iodine, so less thyroid and lung toxicity.
ANDROMEDA and PALLAS: do not use in decompensated heart failure or permanent atrial fibrillation.

steps.tx: **Sotalol** is a nonselective beta blocker that also blocks the rapid delayed rectifier, IKr, so it is both class 2 and class 3. **Reverse use dependence** means that potassium block, and QT lengthening, grows as the rate falls, which is the opposite of class 1 use dependence. Start it in hospital on telemetry. Stop it, and check potassium and magnesium, if the QTc stretches or if polymorphic ventricular tachycardia appears. A twisting wide complex rhythm is torsades until proved otherwise.
steps.say: Sotalol is a nonselective beta blocker that also blocks the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current, so it is both class 2 and class 3. Reverse use dependence means the QT effect grows as the heart rate falls. Start it in hospital on telemetry, and treat a polymorphic wide complex rhythm as torsades until proved otherwise.

vis.alt: Electrocardiogram of a rapid irregular wide complex rhythm whose QRS height changes from beat to beat.
vis.caption: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, the rhythm class 3 drugs can provoke. Image: Panthro, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: **Dofetilide** is a **pure selective IKr** blocker, without the beta blocking or sodium blocking baggage of sotalol or amiodarone. The kidney clears it, so the dose is chosen from creatinine clearance and then checked in hospital with serial QT measurements. Unlike class 1c drugs, it is accepted in patients with heart failure or a low ejection fraction, provided the QT and the potassium stay in range. Outpatient initiation is not appropriate.
steps.say: Dofetilide is a pure selective blocker of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current, without clinically useful beta blockade. The kidney clears it, so the dose follows creatinine clearance and is started in hospital with serial QT checks. It may be used in heart failure when the QT and the potassium stay safe.

rows: Careful. Reverse use dependence and QT risk
Acceptable if QT and potassium are watched

steps.tx: **Adenosine** binds **A1 adenosine receptors** on the atrioventricular node. A G protein then opens an inward rectifier potassium current, the node hyperpolarises, and a circuit that needs the node stops at once. The half life is under 10 seconds, so the effect is gone before most infusions finish. It is the drug for atrioventricular nodal re entry. It does not terminate ventricular tachycardia, and in pre excited atrial fibrillation it can speed conduction down an accessory path.
steps.say: Adenosine binds A1 adenosine receptors on the atrioventricular node, opens a potassium current, and hyperpolarises the node so a circuit that needs the node stops. The half life is under 10 seconds. It terminates atrioventricular nodal re entry. It does not treat ventricular tachycardia, and it is dangerous in pre excited atrial fibrillation.

steps.tx: **Ibutilide** is an intravenous **Class III agent** used to stop atrial flutter or recent atrial fibrillation when a shock is not the first move. It increases a slow inward sodium current and blocks delayed rectifier potassium channels, so the action potential and the QT both lengthen. That is the same reason torsades follows a few percent of infusions. Give it where the rhythm can be defibrillated, keep potassium and magnesium normal, and watch the monitor for several hours after the dose.
steps.say: Ibutilide is an intravenous class 3 agent used to stop atrial flutter or recent atrial fibrillation. It promotes a slow inward sodium current and blocks potassium channels, so the action potential and the QT both lengthen. Give it where the rhythm can be defibrillated, and watch the monitor for torsades for several hours.

vis.alt: Ventricular action potential. The dotted trace repolarises later than the solid trace, which is the effect of blocking the delayed potassium current.
vis.caption: Delayed repolarisation, the ibutilide effect that lengthens the QT. Image: Ksheka, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.
